databases.name: postgres
databases.title: PostgreSQL
databases.note: Rehearsal, advisory locks, and transactional DDL all run here. Enum ADD VALUE inside a transaction sets the floor.

databases.name: mysql
databases.title: MySQL
databases.note: No transactional DDL, so rehearse needs scratch=True. ALTER TABLE DROP CONSTRAINT sets the floor.

databases.name: mariadb
databases.title: MariaDB
databases.note: Same dialect as MySQL. SKIP LOCKED sets the floor. JSON columns read back through their json_valid check.

databases.name: mssql
databases.title: SQL Server
databases.note: Off the rehearsal allowlist, so rehearse refuses without scratch=True. OFFSET with FETCH sets the floor. pyodbc needs the ODBC driver installed.

databases.name: presto
databases.title: Presto and Trino
databases.note: Reads the tpch catalog. Neither server takes the migration surface. The floor is the first release under the Trino name; PrestoDB works for the surface its engine has, untested here.

databases.name: sqlite
databases.title: SQLite
databases.note: Standard library. The table rebuild path lives here. RETURNING and DROP COLUMN set the floor; sqlite3.sqlite_version says what your Python links.

databases.name: duckdb
databases.title: DuckDB
databases.note: In-process, so no container and no advisory lock. Releases before 1.0 are not claimed.

databases.name: athena
databases.title: AWS Athena
databases.note: Your AWS account, with a staging S3 directory. Iceberg MERGE sets the floor at engine version 3. Athena's migration surface is not exercised, since the tables it needs live in your buckets.

databases.name: default
databases.title: ANSI (default)
databases.note: The portable compiler. Any DB-API 2.0 driver that takes this SQL will work, untested here.
